subject.title: [Bug]: codex harness mirrored-session-history read fails for ephemeral sessions and on failover; one-shot cleanup retires shared app-server client while turns are in flight

question: Should OpenClaw treat Codex app-server rollout JSONL as a supported transcript source for harness/failover context, or should unsupported Codex rollout shapes be skipped as debug-only metadata?
rationale: Both choices are technically plausible, but they set different product contracts for transcript ownership, fallback memory, warning behavior, and cross-provider recovery.

options.title: Support Codex rollout history
options.body: Parse Codex session_meta/response_item rollout files into the harness context where safe, and add focused coverage for ephemeral and failover paths.

options.title: Skip unsupported shapes quietly
options.body: Downgrade Codex rollout-shaped files to structured debug metadata and keep fallback/session continuity anchored only on OpenClaw-native transcripts.

options.title: Split active-memory only
options.body: Track the active-memory zero-message timeout separately and leave broader Codex fallback transcript semantics unresolved for now.

recommendation.title: Support Codex rollout history
recommendation.body: Parse Codex session_meta/response_item rollout files into the harness context where safe, and add focused coverage for ephemeral and failover paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses product/runtime boundaries and steipete is a recent adjacent contributor on Codex replay plus current checked-out affected lines.
